name: Pablo Quintana
equipment: Buckskin coat, short, over a striped wool shirt, a red sash and leather leggings
Carbine (Spencer, .56-50), in a scabbard on the bell mare's pack saddle
Bullwhip, eighteen feet, for the mules, which he says he has never used on a mule and which is true
Horse: La Campana, his bell mare, who leads a pack train of fourteen mules with aparejo pack saddles
Rope, diamond-hitch cinches, a farrier's kit and a sack of oats
A rosary, a Santo Niño de Atocha medal, and a letter from his wife Lupe in Taos
A ledger of every load he has packed over Hollowell Pass this year and who paid for it
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: he speaks English and Spanish natively, knows every trail and town of northern New Mexico and the San Luis Valley, and has advantage on Persuasion and Insight checks with people who live along the border, of either side)

Saddle-Born (Cowhand: advantage on Riding checks, no disadvantage on ranged attacks from the saddle, mounts or dismounts with 5 ft of movement. La Campana is part of him: she has extra hit points equal to 5 x his cowhand level, never spooks under him, comes to his whistle from half a mile, and the mules follow her bell. Lariat: proficient, and from the saddle he throws a loop as a bonus action)
Rawhide (Cowhand: advantage on saves against exhaustion, heat and cold; he rides 12 hours a day without forced-march saves and spends one extra Hit Die on a short rest)
Cow Sense (Cowhand, 2nd level: advantage on Animal Handling with cattle, horses and mules; he turns a stampede's leaders with one check as an action, with advantage)

Outfit: Trail Hand (Cowhand, 3rd level: he moves a pack train or a herd at 12 to 15 miles a day over any trail a mule can stand on, and his outfit has advantage on night-watch Perception checks and river crossings)
Proving Up (Homesteader background: his family has farmed the Taos valley for six generations; every Hispano farm, church and packers' corral from Taos to Conejos will feed him and tell him the news)

personality.traits: I am cheerful, superstitious and talkative, and I sing to the mules in the morning. I know everybody's business on every trail and I tell all of it.
personality.ideals: Work is honest when the pay is honest. The railroad will put me out of business, and I will still help it, because a man has to live in the century he is in.
personality.bonds: Lupe and our four children in Taos, and the adobe house I am building them a room at a time. My mules, every one of whom has a name and a saint. Pepa Archuleta, whose father taught me to throw a diamond hitch.
personality.flaws: I rent my mules to anyone who pays in coin and I do not ask questions. Usually that is good business.

appearance: A stocky, cheerful Nuevomexicano of thirty-three with a round brown face, a magnificent drooping moustache, a straw sombrero with a red band and a coat that smells of mules. He laughs with his whole body and never stops moving.
backstory: Pablo Quintana was born in the Taos valley, where his family have farmed for six generations, and he has packed freight on mules since he was twelve: Santa Fe, the San Juan mines, Leadville, and since the spring, every pick, keg and bale that comes over Hollowell Pass to Argent faster than the railroads can bring it. The DA&P's tie-cutting and grading crews are full of men from his part of New Mexico, and their spokesman Teodoro Gallegos is his wife's cousin. When the first train runs his business is over, and he is sad about it and has decided to be practical: he has a contract to pack supplies to the railroad's construction camps until the snow. He knows every trail over the pass, including a few the surveyors never found.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Pablo is the party's legs and ears on the trails, and their way into the Hispano crews of the DA&P. He can get them anywhere a mule can go, faster than the wagon road, and he is the cheerful, gossiping counterweight to the heavier companions. In sl-scenario-002 he can take them up to the rockslide and over to the GP&P railhead at Burnt Mule Flats by a back trail. In sl-scenario-004 his pack trail is the way around the Narrows and the way to carry recovered silver if the railroad cannot.
dmNotes.voice: Fast, warm, mixed English and Spanish: ay, compadre, ¡qué barbaridad!, mira. He names every mule and talks about them like people. Swears by saints. Laughs at his own jokes before he finishes them.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get through the season with his mules and his contract and go home to Taos before the snow. Secondary: see the Hispano crews paid in coin, not scrip. Tertiary: stay out of trouble, which he is bad at.
dmNotes.secrets: On Tuesday afternoon he rented three mules and pack saddles to Tobe Kersey, the DA&P brakeman, who said it was for a prospecting party and paid $15 in gold coin, which is more than Tobe makes in a week. The mules came back to the corral on Wednesday morning with no one leading them and fresh scratches from a narrow trail. He has said nothing, because he is afraid he rented mules to whoever stole the DA&P dynamite on Tuesday night (he did), and the Miners' Union would like any excuse to run Mexicans out of the basin too (Clue G1b; he gives it up to Pepa Archuleta at once, or to anyone who promises to keep his name out of it).
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: instantly friendly, a little too talkative. Toward Pepa Archuleta: an uncle's pride, and fear of her temper. Toward Ong Pak-wai: professional respect; they share a campfire at the Cut and a low opinion of the Miners' Union. Toward Teodoro Gallegos: family. Toward the railroads: both of them will ruin him, and he likes Coburn better.
